v01: Twenty Keynote slides, built one element at a time: 81 tool calls.
v02: mcp-keynote builds the whole deck from one spec, in one call.
v03: Claude writes one spec: slides, tables, charts, notes and transitions.
v04: The server checks all of it before anything is created.
v05: A typo or an invented key comes back named, with what to use instead.
v06: Your text reaches AppleScript as arguments, never pasted into the script,
v07: so a title full of quotes can't break it, or take it over.
v08: Then Keynote builds native tables with live formulas, 17 chart types and styled connectors,
v09: and exports to PDF, PowerPoint, a movie or HTML.
v10: describe_deck reads an open deck back into the same spec, ready to diff in git.
v12: On a real Keynote, 289 live checks ran: none failed.
v13: It rebuilds ByAxe's keynote-mcp, a fork of easychen's original.
v14: mcp-keynote. Keynote decks, built from one declarative spec.
